question.text: Diraq/UNSW reported control fidelities above 99% across four silicon spin-qubit devices fabricated in a 300-millimetre commercial semiconductor foundry — imec, not a university cleanroom. What does 'unit cells exceeding 99% fidelity' establish?
options: That industrial fabrication of a handful of qubits at a time can hit fidelities comparable to bespoke lab devices — not that wiring and crosstalk stay manageable at the qubit counts leading modalities have reached
That silicon spin qubits fabricated this way can now be scaled to hundreds of qubits without new engineering challenges
That fidelity above 99% has been demonstrated at the same qubit count as the leading superconducting processors
That imec's foundry process is now the industry-standard way every quantum computer is manufactured
question.hint: 'Unit cell' is doing a lot of work in that phrase. How many qubits does a unit cell actually contain?

explain.g: The headline result here is about manufacturing, not qubit count: a commercial chip foundry, not a university lab, produced small groups of qubits that perform this well. That's genuinely significant for whether this technology could ever be mass-produced — but it doesn't say anything about what happens when you wire hundreds of these together, which is a different and much less tested problem.
explain.y: Steinacker, Dumoulin Stuyck, Lim, Tanttu, Feng et al., Nature 646, 81–87 (2025) reports single- and two-qubit control fidelities above 99% across all four devices tested, with state-preparation-and-measurement fidelity up to 99.9% — but 'unit cells' means a handful of qubits per device, fabricated in a 300mm imec line rather than a bespoke cleanroom. None of this is at the qubit counts the leading modalities (superconducting, trapped-ion) have reached.
explain.r: The thesis under test is industrial-scale fabrication compatibility, not qubit-count scaling — those are separate axes. Whether control wiring, crosstalk and calibration overhead stay manageable as unit-cell counts climb from a handful to hundreds is explicitly untested by this result, and is the open question the source paper itself frames the work around.
